We had a wonderful experience with this clinic. Our dog ate some bad food and became very sick—she was shaking, vomiting, and clearly not feeling well—so we rushed her to the nearest veterinarian.

The staff was able to see us right away, and the veterinarian spoke excellent English, which was incredibly reassuring while traveling abroad. She immediately put us at ease, explained that everything would be okay, and acted quickly to help our baby.

Our dog started feeling better within minutes. The doctor administered a medication to calm her stomach, provided a probiotic for us to continue giving her at home, and advised us on a safe diet while she recovered.

Thanks to their prompt care and compassion, we were able to continue our trip knowing our dog was safe, comfortable, and well cared for. She remained healthy from that point forward. We are extremely grateful for the excellent care and would highly recommend this clinic to anyone needing veterinary services.

She has a holistic approach and, in addition to being a veterinarian, she treats with homeopathy, acupuncture, and is trained as an energy healer. I searched for a long time before finding her in Paris, and I am so relieved because she has unique skills and has given me hope. My cat, who is still young, suffers from chronic back pain that causes constipation and urinary problems, and conventional medicine only offers injections which, in the long term, can have serious and irreversible side effects.

Consultation for our rabbit. We had booked an appointment on the website, selecting a vet who was supposed to be knowledgeable about exotic pets. They are fragile animals, and we were looking for good advice, an expert opinion… We found none of that.

Basically, the session boiled down to, “If he poops, eats, and is active, everything is fine.” Yet our rabbit had several worrying symptoms… But never mind.

Then, we wanted to ask about our rabbit’s (encephalitozoon) cuniculi, and the vet had to look it up online… It’s a serious condition that affects almost 75% of domestic rabbits! So we gave up on getting any advice on that.

Then, at the end of the consultation, the vet gave us a sheet with “recommended” foods for rabbits… On it were grains that are STRONGLY discouraged for exotic pets. I want to reiterate that the goal of the appointment was to treat our rabbit, not to make things worse.

Anyway, the following week, we went to another clinic where a wonderful vet was able to reassure us and diagnose our rabbit's health problems: a nasty dental and skin infection.

Conclusion: Don't offer services you can't provide. The well-being of our animals is at stake!
